extracted.intended_audience: farmers, landowners, and prospective country-home buyers (especially near New York/Westchester County)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, experience-based guidance for buying, siting, improving, and managing a small farm: selecting a site, woodlot and orchard management, drainage and swamp reclamation, barn siting and construction, and general soil/fertilizer practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-home selection requisites
rubrics_metrics.description: A country home should have three requisites: 1. A peerless spring of pure, soft, living water; 2. A cascade or brawling brook; 3. Woods largely composed of evergreens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These features determined the author's choice of farm and justify choosing a rocky, wooded hillside rather than more fertile but less desirable locations; being near a railroad station and within reasonable distance of the city were also considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and value woodlands (keep ~1/4 in woods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a significant portion of land (about one fourth) in wood, judiciously covering ridges and ravines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Woods protect fields from drought, winds, and protect delicate fruits; stripping land of trees causes erosion, desolating torrents, and poorer crops. Do not recklessly cut and burn forests; instead be saving of timber.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit pasturing in woods
rubrics_metrics.description: Shut cattle out of the greater part of the woods; pasturing woods is a glaring vice of agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cattle browse tender twigs of valuable young trees and leave coarse/unwanted species; excluding cattle increased regeneration (e.g., ten times more Sugar Maple, White Ash).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicious cutting and thinning of trees
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut out trees that stop growing or begin to decay; thin and trim woodlands rather than reckless clearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any fairly grown forest can spare trees and be benefited; thin poorer trees, trim lower limbs, cut out Red Oak and sow White Oak acorns, and when many sprouts start from a stump cut away all but two or three, repeating later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forest cultivation for timber investment
rubrics_metrics.description: Buy sterile tracts and cover them with choice trees (White Oak, Hickory, White Pine, Locust, Chestnut) to grow timber as a profitable long-term investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timber grows dearer over time; near a city, growing timber can be more profitable and safer investment than grain; plant trees on ledges or rocks where tillage is impeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tree-planting as climate mollifier and shelter
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant evergreens as ornamental drapery and as mollifiers of climate—shelter belts and windbreaks increase productive capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evergreen belts warm gardens (several degrees), shelter low ridges and gardens, and improve health and enjoyment for current and future generations; plant a dozen judiciously and shield them from injury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transplanting trees — do not dry roots
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid exposing and drying roots of trees when transplanting; drying roots risks killing the tree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sugar Maples tolerate poor handling better than most; the finer the care (keeping roots moist and shaded) the better the survival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hedge/wind-break planting for garden warming
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant a low ridge or belt of evergreens north of garden as a shelter to raise average temperature and protect early vegetables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copse or clump of evergreens can be 40 rods by 3–4 rods; it materially warms and shelters greenhouses, strawberry beds, grape-vines, and increases productive capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trim and prune for timber quality and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Trim lower limbs and dead spikes, especially on Hemlocks, to improve timber growth and remove hazardous bayonet-like branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim Hemlocks high (e.g., 50 feet) to produce better timber and reclaim ground space; cut away limbs gradually and convert to fuel; trimming accelerates timber value and reduces danger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thin multiple sprouts from stumps
rubrics_metrics.description: When several sprouts start from a single stump, cut away all but two or three, and later thin again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This promotes better growth of remaining sprouts and yields timber more valuable and faster-growing than neglected sucker growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orchard variety strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer planting one variety (e.g., Russet) in an orchard for convenience of gathering and marketing; avoid planting many sorts together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Russets yield bounteously, keep well into April/May, and are less inviting to worms; choose varieties with marketing and storage advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apple-tree planting depth
rubrics_metrics.description: The ground on which Apple-trees are set should be trenched three feet deep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deep trenching and good fertilization set the foundation for productive orchards; the author's ground was not trenched deep enough, though well fertilized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove old, tall, neglected apple trees
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut down old Apple-trees grown too tall, neglected, or producing poor fruit without grafting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tall, uncared-for trees foster caterpillars and are nuisances; cut them down as soon as you can obtain fruit for use elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swamp reclamation: drain thoroughly or convert to cranberry
rubrics_metrics.description: Either thoroughly drain swamps (with adequate fall) or provide for winter flooding and lay them down to cranberries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before draining, be sure of a good outlet and at least two feet fall from lowest point at flood-time; burying tiles where water reverses is unprofitable and discouraging; thorough under-draining is the basis of lasting improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drainage engineering prerequisite — ensure fall
rubrics_metrics.description: Always begin swamp drainage by ensuring a good outlet and sufficient fall — at least two feet from lowest point at flood-time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without adequate fall, drains will choke with back-water, making under-draining ineffective; engage competent engineering when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barn siting for manure and efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the barn on the higher (upper/east) side of the place so manure and heavy materials are easier to draw downhill than up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A barn on a shelf of the hill functions as a manure manufactory; design should consider ease of moving heavy fertilizers and animals' wintering costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barn construction for durability and animal comfort
rubrics_metrics.description: Build barn walls of solid stone or concrete with a good roof (e.g., Vermont slate); include basement for manures, stable for animals, and hayloft above; provide sufficient windows for light and air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solid construction reduces wintering costs (animals kept warmer), and a three-story arrangement (manure cellar, stable, hay story) is practical; more windows improve light and ventilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soil improvement through physical work and fertilizers
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve rocky upland by digging, blasting, picking out rock, running under-drains, ploughing deeper, and persistent fertilizing with composted swamp muck, lime, salt, gypsum, bone-dust, and artificial/mineral manures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated amendments bring poor land into fair condition; additional deepening of six to twelve inches may be needed; roots and many crops do well if ground is properly prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dairy-land phosphate requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Most lands devoted to milk production need phosphates, most readily supplied as ground bones (the finer the better).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplying phosphates restores fertility for grasses and hay critical to dairy production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potato-growing suitability varies by region
rubrics_metrics.description: Potatoes may produce less abundantly on seaboard/southern New York slopes than on breezy mountain slopes or high inland counties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crop suitability must be judged regionally; adapt expectations accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barn as long-term investment and pride
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-built barn (stone walls, slate roof) is an enduring structure providing lasting utility and standing as a testament to the builder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality construction now yields durable benefit beyond the founder's lifetime; think long-term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal oversight required for good labor
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot hire good work unless you give personal attention; a hired man who is not personally supervised will not do efficient work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a worker would be efficient, he'd work his own land; farm profitability depends on better oversight than the author could give while otherwise employed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the axe and physical labor for health and woodland work
rubrics_metrics.description: The axe is an excellent, healthful implement for sedentary workers; habitual use improves posture and health and is suitable for woodland cultivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cutting out trash, trimming trees, and axe work both exercises the body and accomplishes needed woodland management; the author recommends youth learn to love the axe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garden and house siting — avoid over-shaded, damp spots
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid building a house too shaded and shut-in (too damp), which may cause chimney smoke and be unhealthy; balance proximity to spring with exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While shaded plats are cool and quiet, they can be damp and poorly ventilated; a house should have adequate sunlight and dryness for health and comfort.
